title: The 'delivery snap' pin never tests delivery — interp_continuous never reads p.delivered, and a delivered packet at its heading node evaluates continuous-TRUE
evidence: Test sets: "p.delivered = true" then "p.on_edge = false / p.at_node = 2" and asserts "testing.expect(t, !interp_continuous(&topo, 0, 1, 0, true, &p), "delivered transition must snap")". The predicate's only cross-kind branches are: "if entry_on_edge { // arrival: was heading toward the node it now sits at return entry_heading == p.at_node }" — no reference to p.delivered anywhere in interp_continuous. README claims: "every teleport (sever drop-back, ECMP reroute, spawn, delivery) FALSE (the snap)."
detail: The assertion passes only because at_node(2) != entry_heading(1); the delivered flag is inert. A delivered packet resting at its heading node returns TRUE from the predicate, so the advertised 'delivery FALSE' pin is not actually tested.
recommended_fix: Either add an explicit delivered check to interp_continuous (return false when p.delivered) with a test at_node == heading, or rename the test and drop the 'delivery FALSE' claim from README/PR.

title: Trail echoes scale RGB by the fade factor in addition to alpha, contradicting the stated 'packet's own body color at low alpha'
evidence: TRAIL_FADES doc: "// read: the newest echo is the strongest, the oldest is a ghost). Drawn in // the packet's own body color at low alpha — the §4 direction verbatim // ("trail = the packet color at low alpha")." Code: "ebody := rl.Color{u8(f32(body.r) * fade), u8(f32(body.g) * fade), u8(f32(body.b) * fade), u8(f32(body.a) * fade)}"
detail: Both color channels and alpha are multiplied by fade, so echoes render a darkened color, not the body color at low alpha — the field notes' own probe confirms alpha blending works for circles, making the RGB scaling a double-darken.
recommended_fix: Scale only alpha (keep body.r/g/b) to match the quoted §4 direction, or amend the TRAIL_FADES comment and PR body to say 'darkened body color'.

title: Mangled indentation in the motion-strip cadence-export block — the export call sits at the wrong nesting depth
detail: The if-line is over-indented (6 tabs) inside a 4-tab block and its body/closers don't line up; braces balance, but the scope reads wrong on first pass and suggests an unreviewed hand-merge of the W5 fix.
recommended_fix: Reindent the render_strip_frame call and its body to one level inside the `if (t - start_ms) % step_ms == 0` block.

title: motion.dem header calls 2200..2450 'the strip window' while every reproduce command runs 2200..2600
location: demos/motion.dem:header comment vs README.md / pr-body reproduce commands
evidence: demos/motion.dem: "# The 2200..2450ms strip window is therefore the pure mid-edge glide; the # tail of the window (2450ms+) is the post-arrival doorstep phase". README: "./bin/harness motion-strip motion 2200 2600 17 bin/m60-before snapshot"; pr-body: "motion 2200 2600 17 <dir>".
detail: The comment self-contradicts: if the window ended at 2450 there would be no 'tail of the window (2450ms+)'. The actual strip window is 2200..2600; only the glide sub-range is 2200..2450.
recommended_fix: Reword to 'the 2200..2600ms strip window: 2200..2450 is the pure mid-edge glide; 2450+ the post-arrival tail'.

title: --xmax flag without a value crashes measure_packet_motion.py with an unhandled IndexError
detail: A trailing or valueless --xmax raises IndexError (non-numeric value raises ValueError) as a raw traceback, despite the docstring's advertised 'Robustness (Perkins r1 W3/W4/W7/W12)' hardening pass.
recommended_fix: Validate the argument index and int-parse with a clean stderr message and return 2, or switch to argparse for free validation.
